title: Nocturne miniroll sentinel and cost-sampling notes (WIP)
body:
Purpose: lightweight late-evening (nocturne) mini-roll protocol with tight telemetry sampling to validate performance/cost tradeoffs before a daytime ramp. This is intended for incremental feature toggles or small model variant switches where we want strong cost signal without full traffic exposure.

Summary (short):
- Goal: surface correctness, latency, and per-token cost anomalies in a 3-hour night window.
- Window: 23:00–02:00 PT (overnight) — low user traffic.
- Scope: 5% region-local traffic split, 3 model variants (baseline, q8, q5-2), telemetry-driven gating.
- Safety: immediate 30-minute rollback threshold on latency or error-rate regressions; automatic global fallback if cost-per-response > 1.5x baseline for two consecutive samples.

Owners & on-call:
- Release lead: Jordan Patel (owner) — primary contact and approval for ramping.
- Telemetry lead: Sofia Kim — defines signal queries, runs post-launch audit.
- Rollback operator: Marcus Lee (SRE) — executes rollback and coordinates incident comms.
- Cost analytics: Priya Rao (FinOps) — monitoring cost-sampling probes and budget alarms.
- On-call rotation for launch window: Marcus -> Sofia -> Jordan (listed order is escalation).

Preflight checklist (complete 24–2 hours before window):
- [ ] Draft release notes and one-line summary for on-call channel (owner: Jordan).
- [ ] Confirm canary routing rules in routing service (jira: ENGREL-3421) — config review.
- [ ] Verify model artifacts present in model registry (tags: baseline/q8/q5-2) and container images pushed.
- [ ] Run local smoke harness against q8 and q5-2 images (basic generator tests + KV warmup).
- [ ] Run cost-sampling dry run against a replay of 5000 recent requests to validate sampling script.
- [ ] Update traffic-guard config: max-ramps per 30m = 2, max-absolute-traffic = 5% region-local.
- [ ] Confirm alerting thresholds in PagerDuty and Slack (see alerts block below).
- [ ] Confirm runbook links and postmortem template presence.

Launch timeline (hour-by-hour):
- T-90m: final signoff call (15m) — release lead + telemetry lead + SRE + FinOps. Quick checklist run.
- T-60m: deploy variant images to canary pool (no traffic yet). Warm caches (KV prefix warmup 1k requests per variant).
- T-30m: enable cost-sampling probe (background) and start lightweight synthetic generator at 0.1 rps/variant for steady signal.
- T-10m: sample test traffic (100 requests across variants) and validate traces & cost tags.
- T+0: route 1% region-local traffic for 20 minutes. Collect telemetry.
- T+20m: evaluate signals. If green, ramp to 3% for 30 minutes.
- T+50m: evaluate. If green, ramp to 5% for remainder of window.
- T+180m: end window — begin retention checks and schedule next-day daylight probe if needed.

Telemetry & gating signals (primary):
- Latency P95: baseline = 180ms; gate = 180ms + 60ms (i.e., fail if >240ms sustained for two consecutive 10m windows).
- Error rate (5xx + malformed outputs): baseline = 0.4%; gate = >1.2% over a 10m window.
- Throughput loss: if successful token output per request drops below 70% of baseline median for 10m.
- Cost per response (in USD-equivalent from cost probe tags): baseline = $0.012; gate = >$0.018 for two consecutive samples (sample window=10m).
- Quality regression (sampled eval set): BLEU-like or match rates drop >3% vs baseline on the nightly eval set of 200 prompts.

Telemetry sampling plan (cost-focused):
- Probe frequency: every 10 minutes aggregate across all variants.
- Sampled keys: request_id, model_variant, tokens_generated, dec_time_ms, cost_tag_usd, workspace_tier.
- Aggregation dims: variant, region, route. Store 90 days.
- Quick sanity: run a cost-sampling job at T+15m and T+75m that computes per-1000-token USD. Notify FinOps on variance >25%.

Rollback triggers and actions:
- Automatic rollback (immediate):
  - Error rate > 2.5% in a single 5m window.
  - Latency P95 > 350ms sustained 3 consecutive 1m windows.
  - Cost per response > 2x baseline across two consecutive 10m samples.
- Manual rollback (requires release lead):
  - Quality regression flagged by telemetry lead on eval set (drop >5%).
  - SEV triggered by downstream systems (auth, billing) — coordinate with SRE.
- Rollback steps:
  - Rollback operator (Marcus) issues traffic re-route back to baseline variant and disables canary.
  - Post-rollback: run retrospective smoke tests, capture current traces, snapshot cost sample file.
  - Communicate to #release-watch and to stakeholders via one-paragraph update.

Communication templates (Slack):
- Preflight post (template):
  - "Nocturne miniroll window starting 23:00 PT tonight. 5% region-local max. Slack watch channel: #nocturne-watch. If you are on-call, please be reachable. TL;DR: cost probes enabled, telemetry leads: Sofia, Marcus."
- Incident post (template):
  - "[INCIDENT] Nocturne miniroll: rolling back at T+XX due to <signal>. Affected: region X, variant Y. Owner: Jordan Patel. Taking traffic back to baseline. Details: <short list>. Follow-up: postmortem scheduled."

Smoke tests & post-deploy checks (automated):
- End-to-end generation sanity on 50 prompts (pass criteria: no exceptions, outputs length within 30% of baseline, no toxic classification).
- Latency microbenchmark: 1000 fanout requests to measure P50/P95/P99 at canary pool.
- Cache-warmness check: KV hit rate target >= 60% after 30 minutes.
- Telemetry tag presence: every request must have cost_tag_usd and model_variant. Missing tags >2% -> fail.

Nightly post-window audit (next day):
- Telemetry lead runs full 3-hour aggregation and writes a 1-paragraph verdict in this doc (owner: Sofia).
- Cost analytics runs billing-match job that ties sampled cost tags to invoice line items (owner: Priya).
- If cost anomalies appear, schedule a mini postmortem; otherwise, prep for a daytime microramp of up to 15% next day.

Release notes draft (to copy into release channel if green):
- "Nocturne miniroll: Experimental model variants q8 and q5-2 deployed to 5% region-local traffic overnight. Focus: measure cost savings and latency/quality impact. Outcome: preliminary pass/fail summary + link to telemetry snapshot."

Open questions & follow-ups:
- How we handle multi-region divergence in cost (need per-region cost baseline) — action Sofia/Priya.
- Whether to enable payload-sampling of full request bodies for one window to debug quality regressions (privacy considerations).
- Automate ramp decision via a simple circuit-breaker in routing service (longer-term).

Quick links:
- Canary routing config: github.com/redwood-inference/routing/greenhouse-config#nocturne
- Runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/release-runbook
- PagerDuty: Team-Release-Eng (PD escalation policy)

Notes to self: this is intentionally lightweight — the goal is cost signal + safety. If telemetry shows any cross-variant instability, abort day-2 ramps and schedule a full debug session.

Appendix: short checklist (one-line check items for T-10m):
- [ ] All owners on call?
- [ ] Slack watch channel created and pinned?
- [ ] PagerDuty escalation configured?
- [ ] Canary images pushed?
- [ ] KV warmup script ready?
- [ ] Sampling probes enabled?

End.
